packs.title: Iron, Hill and Garden
packs.promise: See three sides of Paris through changing views, small street details and reused spaces.

q.s: Follow a safe crossing and watch a landmark change scale.
st: Choose an open pedestrian route from a Trocadéro viewpoint toward Champ de Mars; Pont d’Iéna is one option only when its crossings are open.
From a safe stationary place before moving, record the Eiffel Tower’s apparent size and one object that frames it.
After the crossing, stop clear of foot traffic and record how the tower and its frame changed. Explain what your movement changed, rather than claiming the tower changed.

q.s: Make a small drawing from the spaces around the tower.
st: Choose a lawful public viewpoint on or beside Champ de Mars where some part of the tower is visible.
Draw only two empty shapes: one between pieces of ironwork and one between the tower and a tree, cloud or building edge. A two-line verbal description works as well.
Give each shape a simple name and note how a small shift of your position changes one of them.

q.s: Read an old rail structure from the street below.
st: Walk or roll a comfortable, open stretch of the public pavement beside the Viaduc des Arts.
Choose three arches with different visible fronts, materials or details. Record one observable difference for each; do not infer a business type from a closed door.
Finish with one sentence explaining how a repeated structure can hold changing uses.

packs.title: Between the Lines
packs.promise: Make a Paris story from courtyard patterns and changing river views.

q.s: Find three ways two very different surfaces share a courtyard.
st: Choose a comfortable, lawful public viewpoint at Louvre Cour Napoléon, public area around the Pyramid, approach from Place du Carrousel. Keep the route through the space clear.
From outside the entrance queues, find a triangular shape in glass, a curved shape in stone, and a reflection that brings the two materials together.
Pick the smallest detail of your three and give it a descriptive name of your own. You need no historical guess or museum ticket.
Save the three observations and your small-detail name.

q.s: Write a four-line scene using only things you can see.
st: Choose a comfortable, lawful public viewpoint at Louvre Cour Carrée, open public courtyard or exterior view from Rue de l’Amiral de Coligny. Keep the route through the space clear.
Choose three visible ingredients from the courtyard facade: an opening, a carved shape, and a patch of light.
Write four short lines: one per ingredient, then a line joining all three.
Keep the four lines in a field note, with an optional architecture photo.

q.s: Turn a short crossing into a changing-view ritual.
st: Choose a comfortable, lawful public viewpoint at Pont des Arts public pedestrian bridge, from Quai François Mitterrand toward Quai de Conti. Keep the route through the space clear.
If the open bridge approach suits you, walk or roll a comfortable portion and pause out of the through route at two or three points. A full crossing is optional.
At each pause choose a river detail: a ripple, a bridge line, a bank, or a changing reflection. Notice which detail changes most as your viewpoint moves.
Save three brief frames in words, or one photo and a note describing the other views.
